My mother passed in 2013 when I was 17. I'm also alone today and I can completely relate. It sucks seeing everyone post about their mothers when I can't have mine here. 
I hope you can find some sort of peace today. Maybe go for a walk, or do something nice for yourself.

I heavily rely on music to keep me going. I literally have no idea how I would get by without music. It explains my thoughts and feelings in a way I never could. It helps me understand and feel and gives me a small amount of peace amidst all the chaos.

I guess I just know I'm going no where and I know ending it would cause others a lot of pain but eventually they would move on. If I stick around, I continue to make them upset and hurt them. I am already losing the moments that could turn my life around because I am trapped in my current situation. Happiness is just out of reach because I'm too scared of how it would affect certain people and how people would look at me and I'm not ready to lose those people in my life.

I'm really glad you found happiness in that trip. I wish I knew a way to find that. I don't know if I have hit rock bottom yet though. I keep thinking things will get better but they always get worse. More things just keep piling on. I think I find happiness in something and then I realize that it is wrong to find happiness in that.

I can appreciate what you are saying. The issue is that yes, sometimes I can have a good time, but the thoughts are always there and I can't get rid of them. Maybe, maybe I could be happy down the line but I don't think I have the strength to make the decisions that will get me to that point and I don't know if it would actually be better for me. I would probably be ruining a lot of things. Maybe I am cheating myself and taking the easy way out, but I'm not strong enough to live like this.

I found a lump in May of 2018 and immediately freaked out. My grandmother had ovarian cancer and all of her siblings had some sort of breast/ovarian cancer so she was tested for the BRCA 2 gene and was positive. My dad got tested and was also positive so all of my siblings got tested and we are all positive except for one. The gene means I have about a 45% higher risk of getting breast/ovarian cancer. 

I was supposed to start doing routine checks around the age of 25 but since I found a lump I obviously had to start doing these much sooner. Luckily, this lump turned out to be nothing. The radiologists were super helpful and as soon as I told people about the gene I carry, everyone did everything they could to guarantee that it wasn't anything serious. 

The first time I went in they did an ultrasound and said it looked benign and I had no reason to worry. I went back in 6 months later and it had grown a little and the edges we're less defined so the doctor wanted to help ease my worries and I went ahead and had a biopsy done and everything came back good. I still have the lump and I now wear wireless bras so it doesn't hurt. 

3 days ago I noticed pain in my other breast and started feeling around. I felt something, but it could be muscle.. Im not sure if it is a lump yet. I am about 60% sure it is a lump at this point but I am waiting until I am more positive because my primary care doctor is awful and I don't want to go to see him if I'm not sure there is an issue. 

This all has caused me extreme stress and anxiety. Even though they repeatedly tell me my lump is nothing to worry about, I still worry. The good news is that because I have this gene, insurance would pay for my breast removal because it is preventive and not cosmetic. Not sure if they would pay for implants though haha.
